metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon: Sawubona (Zulu), one word. Wagwan is Bear's alone.

beats.role_note: WALKER BOOKEND 1/4 - ClaudeComposerAsk. Reconstructed prompt, said aloud to be a reconstruction. Liam named in the first breath.
beats.narration_text: Sawubona - this is Liam, in for Bear. The prompt on screen is a reconstruction. It was written to be illustrative and it is not a transcript. The game under it is real: a dungeon slice in Godot four, and this time the thing we are taking apart is not the game logic. It is the four shaders, and the question of what a hint actually does.

props.topic: WALKER - GODOT SHADERS AND MATERIALS TEARDOWN
props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about The Lost - a side-view dungeon crawler where every hazard announces itself before it can hurt you - into a Godot project, and then help me write the shader that does the announcing by hand, while you write the driver and the tests that prove it.
props.label: RECONSTRUCTION

beats.role_note: WALKER BOOKEND 2/4 - hesitant writer. One working single-word correction, with measured time to complete it.
beats.narration_text: Here is what actually changed. Three shaders, written by hand, line by line. A spike trap that turns - correction - that ramps red across four tenths of a second before it fires. Two materials from one shader on two identical slimes. And a three pixel image, sampled twice through the same file, that settles what source colour does to a number. Ninety-nine automated checks stand behind that, and four deliberate breakages stand behind the checks.

props.title: What was built
lines: 4 mutations, each caught by a different net
Every predicted pixel committed before it was measured
